## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Lolajātaka* (Ja 274) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Set in Jetavana, the story is told by the Buddha concerning a greedy monk (*lolabhikkhu*) [Fausböll 1879; SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded by SuttaCentral, the Master observes that the monk was greedy in a past existence as well, when his greed cost him his life and drove wise men from home [SuttaCentral]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the tale preserved in the edition of Fausböll, the greedy monk is identified as having been a greedy crow (*lolakāko*) who died groaning at the scene, whereas the Bodhisatta was a pigeon (*pārāpato*) who abandoned the dwelling and flew elsewhere; upon hearing the exposition of the four truths, the greedy monk attained the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].
In the commentary's uddāna summary, the text is cataloged as part of the *Araññavagga* [Fausböll 1879]. Automatic text-reuse data from DharmaNexus shows that the text shares five passages (476 characters) with the second volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0513a2), with the longest segment matching at §2.2–3.4 with 93% similarity [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects minor cross-language alignments with Tibetan texts, including the *Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā-mahāyānasūtra* (D0062), though these represent low-scoring automatic alignments rather than curated parallels [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral].
